analysis.title: US Weekly Kickstart: The equity index impact of SpaceX inclusion so far
key_insights: SpaceX's free float has risen to nearly a third of shares, up from 5% at IPO, nearly five months after the largest US IPO on record. Based on the lockup schedule, about half of shares should be in the float by mid-2027, consistent with precedent from large IPOs with low initial floats.

SpaceX's weight in US equity indices has risen with its free float and should keep rising as float grows and indices rebalance. Most large US indices weight constituents in proportion to free float market cap, so the low float at launch kept its weight small for the first few months.

The Nasdaq-100 is the exception where rising float has a muted mechanical effect. After a methodology change this year, constituents with float below 33% are weighted at 3x float market cap. Above 33% float, the full listed market cap is used.

SpaceX is not in the S&P 500 because of the index's seasoning (12 months public) and profitability (positive GAAP net income for the latest quarter and the trailing four quarters) requirements. On consensus forecasts the profitability test is met once Q2 2027 results are reported, pointing to possible inclusion in H2 2027 unless a corporate action accelerates it. A merger with a current constituent would be reviewed case by case.

Passive ETFs owned about $30 billion of SpaceX at the end of October (about 1.5% of market cap), with about $20 billion tied to Nasdaq-100 benchmarked funds. GS expects modest further increases in index weights from upcoming rebalances.
The next Russell 1000 Growth rebalance is on December 11. GS estimates that if the index rebalanced today it would create over $10 billion of additional passive ETF demand for SpaceX.

Insiders and stakeholders likely remain the largest owners. At the end of June, hedge funds, mutual funds and ETFs held about 5% of market cap, insiders and stakeholders about 70%, and non-filers (mostly individuals) about 25%. Q3 13F filings are due later this month.

The S&P 500 traded roughly flat in the few weeks around the five largest IPOs of the past 30 years before resuming its uptrend, and SpaceX followed a similar pattern. GS cautions that the sample is small and that June's market was affected by other factors.

SpaceX's effect on Nasdaq-100 fundamentals has been small. Excluding it, the index P/E would be less than half a turn lower (19.2x vs 19.5x), and return, volatility and concentration are close to unchanged. GS compares this to Tesla's minor valuation impact on the S&P 500 after its 2020 inclusion.
S&P 500 Q3 2026 earnings season: 88% of companies have reported (439 of 500). Equal-weighted, 62% beat on EPS and 8% missed, against 69% and 7% in Q2 2026. Cap-weighted, 60% beat and 13% missed.

GS keeps its S&P 500 target at 8000 for year-end 2026 (9% above the current 7354) and 8700 at 12 months (18% upside). GS EPS forecasts are $375 for 2026 (+36%), $415 for 2027 (+11%) and $460 for 2028 (+11%). Bottom-up consensus is $369, $426 and $497.

The S&P 500 fell 4.7% this week and the Nasdaq-100 has fallen 10.3% since SpaceX's inclusion. Information Technology fell 12.0% on the week and Semiconductors fell 19.7%. Consumer Staples (+3.6%) and Real Estate (+2.5%) led.

Sentiment and positioning: the GS US Equity Sentiment Indicator reads 0.6, short of the 1.0 level that marks stretched positioning. The S&P 500 forward P/E is 18x. Top-10 concentration is 39% of market cap and 33% of earnings.
GS forecasts the US 10-year yield at 4.8% over 3 and 6 months, falling to 4.5% at 12 months. Brent is forecast to fall from $98 to $80 and COMEX gold to rise from $4,114 to $4,600 over 12 months.
Thematic baskets were hit hard this week: Long vs Short Duration -15.9%, Dual Beta -17.3%, Interest Rate Sensitive -12.6%, Hedge Fund VIP -8.7%. Mutual Fund Over- vs Underweights rose 8.5%.

Fell 12.0% on the week and 16% over 1 month, and is 36% of the S&P 500. GS consensus-based EPS growth is 63-68% for 2026.

earnings_insights: S&P 500 Q3 2026 results as of November 6: 439 of 500 companies (88%) reported. Equal-weighted, 62% beat EPS, 8% missed and 30% were in line, with an average EPS surprise of 7% and a revenue surprise of 2%. All figures are reported actuals.
Cap-weighted, 60% of S&P 500 companies beat on EPS and 13% missed, with an average surprise of 2%. Communication Services is the weak spot, with 17% beating and 81% missing on a cap-weighted basis.
Information Technology has the strongest Q3 beat rate among sectors: 80% beat equal-weighted and 95% cap-weighted. Real Estate (30%) and Materials (29%) were lowest equal-weighted.
Consensus (bottom-up) S&P 500 EPS is $369 for 2026 (+34% y/y) and $426 for 2027 (+16%). The GS forecast is $375 (+36%) and $415 (+11%). These are forecasts.
Consensus 2027 growth for the Nasdaq-100 is 21% sales and 25% earnings. Excluding SpaceX it is 20% and 24%. These are forecasts.

risk_factors: Index weight and passive demand for SpaceX will keep rising with float, including more than $10B of passive demand at the December 11 Russell 1000 Growth rebalance.
Eventual S&P 500 inclusion, possibly H2 2027, would add passive demand and could come sooner through a corporate action such as a merger with a current constituent.
Sharp one-week drawdowns in semiconductors (-19.7%), tech hardware (-7.7%) and long-duration and rate-sensitive baskets show how exposed index returns are to the tech and rates complex.
The comparison set of large IPOs is small and June's market had other drivers, so the historical read-across for SpaceX is weak.

S&P 500 market breadth is narrow by GS's measure, which compares the index's distance from its 52-week high with that of the median stock.
Top-10 concentration in the S&P 500 is 39% of market cap and 33% of forward earnings. The Nasdaq-100 top 10 is 50% of the index and the top 20 is 67% (64% excluding SpaceX).

tension_points.bull_case: SpaceX has had a small effect on Nasdaq-100 valuation, return, volatility and concentration (P/E 19.5x vs 19.2x excluding it), so the IPO has not distorted index fundamentals.
tension_points.bear_case: Float is rising from 5% toward about half by mid-2027, index weights and passive ownership will keep growing, and S&P 500 inclusion could add demand from H2 2027.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Inclusion in the S&P 500 sooner than H2 2027 through a corporate action such as a merger with a current constituent.

theme_stances.key_argument: SpaceX has had a much smaller impact on equity index performance, concentration and valuation than many investors expected.
